title: GPU budget slicing and tail-margin strategy for mixed weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and validate a pragmatic GPU memory budgeting approach that slices available device memory across three competing consumers (model weights, KV cache, activations) and preserves a small dynamic tail margin for continuous-batching spikes. This ticket covers design, simulator experiments, and an initial runtime prototype for the margin-slicing policy (aka 'tail-margin slice' or TMS).

Motivation:
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but produces bursty activation peaks that can collide with large KV caches and pinned model weights.
- Existing static quotas either waste headroom (hurting throughput) or lead to OOM events during burst tails.
- We need a policy that is: (a) predictable (bounded OOM risk), (b) low overhead, (c) integrates with KV cache eviction heuristics and autoscaler signals.

Success criteria:
- Simulator shows <0.1% OOM probability on historical mixed workloads while increasing average batch size by >=12% vs baseline static-split.
- Runtime prototype avoids >95% of observed tail-induced preemptions in 72h soak.
- Telemetry added to Console: per-tenant memory slice, tail-margin utilization, eviction events, and p99 latency delta.

Approach overview:
1) Measurement: synthesize mixed traces (short + long context chats + embedding spikes) using traces from trace-replay service (s3://redwood-traces/march-2026/mixed-workloads).
2) Simulator: extend the existing memory-sim harness to simulate TMS policy (fractional slices + reclaimable tail buffer). Key knobs: base-slice-ratios, tail-margin-percentile (p95/p99), reclaim-window-ms, eviction-latency-ms cap.
3) Policy rules (runtime):
   - Reserve: static reservations for weights (pin by model version) + a configurable minimum KV floor.
   - Slice: compute remaining device memory M_rem and divide into slices: S_kv, S_act, S_tail where S_tail := max(dynamic-min, alpha * variance-estimate).
   - Reclaim: when act or kv exceeds slice, start controlled reclamation: prioritize KV partial eviction (LRU-K) then soft-evict activations from long-idle sessions (checkpointing option).
   - Fallback: if reclamation fails, fallback to a smaller model-variant (quantized) or route requests to a lower-cost pool (policy routing).
4) Integration: wire signals to autoscaler (if tail-margin sustained > threshold for 30s trigger burst-scale) and Console metrics.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive tail buffer reduces OOMs but decreases steady-state throughput. We bias buffer sizing toward variance-aware minimal sizing to reclaim when rare.
- Evicting KV aggressively improves activation headroom but can regress generation latency due to cache misses; we limit eviction rate to keep p50 latency impact <5%.
- Checkpointing activations introduces CPU/PCIe overhead; used only as last resort for sessions flagged as long-tail.

Open questions for review:
- Default alpha for tail-margin: start 0.05 (5% of M_rem) or 0.02? Simulation will validate.
- Eviction ordering between KV and activations for multi-tenant GPUs: should we prefer tenant-priority hints? (proposal: use tenant_protection_score + age).

Deliverables:
- Simulator branch with TMS model and a set of reproducible experiments (PR: github.com/redwood/research/pulls/678).
- Design doc: Confluence /docs/runtime/tms-memory-slicing (link below).
- Runtime prototype in serving-runtime: feature gate 'tms_budget_v1' and metrics export.
- Console dashboard draft for per-tenant slice visualization.
